mass.label: Mass
mass.what: Launch mass: the dry spacecraft plus its propellant.
mass.why: Heavier craft need more propellant and a bigger rocket.
mass.real: 1 unit ≈ 10.9 kg. The real orbiter weighed 2,180 kg at launch (JPL MRO press kit).

power.label: Power
power.what: Power the instruments and systems use, against what the solar array makes at Mars.
power.why: Sunlight at Mars is weaker, so every watt costs array area and mass.
power.real: 1 unit ≈ 20 W. The real arrays gave about 2,000 W at Mars (JPL MRO press kit).

data.label: Data
data.what: Data the instruments make, against what the antenna can send home.
data.why: Data that never reaches Earth never becomes science.
data.real: 1 unit ≈ 0.06 Mbps. The real orbiter could send up to 6 Mbps (JPL MRO press kit).

prop.label: Propellant
prop.what: Propellant needed to slow into Mars orbit, against tank size.
prop.why: Propellant is mass too, so extra mass needs extra propellant.
prop.real: 1 unit ≈ 12.2 kg of hydrazine. The real tank held 1,220 kg (JPL MRO press kit).

budget.label: Budget
budget.what: Money spent, against the mission budget.
budget.why: Parts, the rocket and operations all come from one budget.
budget.real: 1 unit = $1 million. The real mission cost about $720 million (JPL MRO press kit).
